title: A conditional pressure-probability predictor against climatology on the knowledge holdouts (#372)
status: A declaration for a reported-only study. It decides nothing and moves no published figure.

holdout_windows.note: Boundaries and checksums are the file's. The script refuses a window whose checksum is not the file's.

gbm_published_4.kind: uncalibrated gbm on the four features of exceedance_gbm.json

gbm_published_9.kind: uncalibrated gbm on the nine features of the funding declaration the published calibrated model reads

dynamic_logit.kind: the frozen dynamic logit of #137 (ml.DYNAMIC_LOGIT_SETTINGS), no recalibration

probit_literature.kind: ridge probit of the label at each threshold (ml.pressure_probit_exceedance, ml.PRESSURE_PROBIT_SETTINGS), uncalibrated
probit_literature.source: docs/pivot/literature.md: Copeland, Duffie & Yang (SR 974) and Ferris, Rose & Tase, a probit on settlement timing and reserve-demand state
probit_literature.fit: the six features of the dynamic logit: spread, month-end, quarter-end, tax-date and coupon-settlement timing, and reserve balances

quantile_literature.kind: linear quantile regressions of the spread read as an exceedance curve (ml.pressure_quantile_exceedance, ml.PRESSURE_QUANTILE_SETTINGS), uncalibrated
quantile_literature.source: docs/pivot/literature.md: Copeland, Duffie & Yang (SR 974); Adrian, Boyarchenko & Giannone (quantile grid smoothed to P(>= x))
quantile_literature.fit: the same six features; the curve at tau is 1 - F(floor(tau) + 0.5), F linear between the grid's quantiles

predictors.fit_failure_rule: A declared predictor whose fit cannot be made on a window (a ValueError from its fit) is reported in the result with the reason and scored on no day; it is never dropped silently.
predictors.note: No published (calibrated) model is held out from these windows: the published records train on every crisis day once it is past. Every figure is labelled uncalibrated.

thresholds.pressure_rule: whole basis points, strictly greater than (docs/decisions/pressure-probability.md)

plain_leap.rule: round(s_t) - round(s_anchor) strictly greater than the jump, anchor as-of (onset.LeapTargets)

leap_benchmarks.climatology: the pooled leap frequency among the training days (every day before the window with an admissible as-of anchor)
leap_benchmarks.persistence_logistic: onset.leap_persistence_logistic: a logistic of the leap on the latest as-of jump and spread, fitted on the same training days
leap_benchmarks.note: A spread-level climatology curve is not a leap climatology, so the leap is benchmarked by these two, not by the pressure benchmarks' curves.

plain_leap.predictor_reading: A predictor's curve is read, for each day, at that day's leap level: floor(round(s_anchor) + jump) + 0.5 bp (onset.LeapTargets.event_threshold). The curve is requested at those levels together with +5 and +10 bp.

score: Brier, per day; paired difference = benchmark Brier minus predictor Brier, positive favours the predictor
splits: leap at-risk days and leap-onset events (onset.LeapTargets)

pass_rule.cell: one predictor at one threshold against one benchmark
met_when: the pooled paired Brier difference has its 90% interval above zero against climatology AND against persistence_logistic
no regime cell and no pressure-day-type cell has its 90% interval wholly below zero against either benchmark; a cell whose interval cannot be bootstrapped is reported and does not count
pass_rule.not_met: reported as not met; a point estimate favouring the predictor with an interval including zero is inconclusive
pass_rule.if_met: nothing is published here. A publish follows docs/decisions/publish-rule.md: paired against the current published declaration on days before 2026-01-01, interval above zero, no regime or day-type cell worse beyond its interval. The live record is not changed.

lockbox: Every scored day is in a window before 2026-01-01. lockbox.require_unlocked checks it before any read or fit.
final_test_groups: The final test's leap-onset and at-risk groups (docs/runs/final_test_near_blind.json) are reported as definitions applied to the holdout days, with day and event counts. That record is read for its group definitions, never rescored.

metrics_beside_brier.source: docs/pivot/literature.md: Alessi & Detken (2011), Sarlin (2013), Drehmann & Juselius (2014), early-warning evaluation
metrics_beside_brier.scope: Every predictor, each target, pooled over the scored days, beside the Brier. Descriptive: they carry no interval and enter no pass rule.
metrics_beside_brier.auroc: Mann-Whitney area under the ROC of the forecast against the outcome, ties counting one half; null when a class is empty.

usefulness.rule: Sarlin (2013): loss(theta) = mu * missed-event rate + (1 - mu) * false-alarm rate for the alarm 'forecast >= theta'; absolute usefulness = min(mu, 1 - mu) - min over theta of loss; relative usefulness = absolute / min(mu, 1 - mu).
usefulness.theta: every forecast value of the predictor on the scored days. The minimum is in-sample on these days, so it is optimistic and is reported as such.

lead_time.rule: pressure.lead_times at the single horizon of this study (h = 1): the lead of an onset is 1 business day when the forecast of it reached the alarm level, else 0; onsets are pressure.onsets at the target's level (pressure targets) and the leap-onset events (the leap).
lead_time.limit: Longer leads need forecasts at longer horizons, which this study does not make; the figure is the share of onsets flagged one business day ahead, and is empty where a target has no onset on the scored days.

scope_ruling: Eleonora, 7 October 2026 (comment on #372): include the literature-scan methods among the predictors where they fit, and report AUROC, usefulness and lead time beside Brier.
